summary: Configured a nightly backup on node1 (cron, 02:30 daily) that SSHes into node2, tars /srv/inventory/data, and stores a dated gzip archive at /var/backups/inventory/inventory-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz, pruning archives older than 7 days. Verified data flow, archive integrity, and retention pruning boundary. Completed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on both nodes with proof of changed boot identity and full post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2: found /srv/inventory/data absent on node2, /var/backups/inventory absent on node1; both nodes CentOS Stream 10 with ssh, rsync, sshd, crond available
Created representative source data at /srv/inventory/data on node2 (item_1.txt..item_3.txt) since the source path did not pre-exist
Installed the cluster shared keypair for passwordless root SSH from node1 to node2 and verified connectivity

Wrote /usr/local/sbin/inventory-backup.sh on node1: streams a tar of node2:/srv/inventory/data over SSH, writes /var/backups/inventory/inventory-<date>.tar.gz, logs to /var/log/inventory-backup.log, and prunes archives older than 7 days
Installed /etc/cron.d/inventory-backup to run nightly at 02:30 as root; confirmed crond active
Ran the backup script manually; verified archive created and contents match source data via extraction
Simulated 8 stale (>7 day old) archives, re-ran the script, confirmed all 8 were deleted and only the current day's archive remained
Simulated a 5-day-old archive (within retention), confirmed it was retained, then removed the synthetic test file
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, uptime, service status, cron file, backup archive, script checksum) on node1 and node2

Restarted node1 via backgrounded systemctl reboot so ack returned before disconnect; polled until reachable; confirmed new boot_id and fresh uptime; verified crond/sshd active, cron file and archive intact, script unchanged, SSH to node2 still functional
Restarted node2 the same way; polled until reachable; confirmed new boot_id and fresh uptime; verified sshd active and source data intact
Re-ran the backup script end-to-end after both restarts to prove the full pipeline still functions

evidence.requirement: Nightly backup script exists and correctly copies node2 data to dated archive on node1
evidence.summary: Script written on node1, executed successfully, and archive contents verified to match source data via extraction and diff of file content
/etc/cron.d/inventory-backup installed with 02:30 daily schedule; crond confirmed active
8 synthetic archives older than 7 days were all deleted on script run; a 5-day-old archive was correctly retained, proving the retention boundary works both directions
Captured boot_id 45c22b1f..., uptime, active crond/sshd, cron file, archive, script checksum

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; node unreachable during reboot; new boot_id ecfabf1a... and fresh uptime confirmed after recovery
crond/sshd active, cron file and prior backup archive intact, script checksum unchanged, SSH to node2 still functional
Captured boot_id bccb87ac..., uptime, active sshd, source data files present

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; node unreachable during reboot; new boot_id d1f51986... and fresh uptime confirmed after recovery

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery and full pipeline verification
evidence.summary: sshd active and source data intact on node2; full backup pipeline re-run from node1 after both restarts succeeded end-to-end
